p1_geometric_convergence.description: Recovering trajectories should show geometric (exponential) convergence, not linear
p1_geometric_convergence.note: All 3 recovering trajectories fit linear better than geometric

p2_basin_boundary.description: Perturbation magnitude should predict basin exit (divergence vs recovery)
p2_basin_boundary.note: Diverging trajectories have lower Jaccard (bigger perturbation) — basin boundary exists

p3_rate_stability.description: Recovery rate should correlate with pre-perturbation stability (Jacobian spectral radius)
p3_rate_stability.note: Pre-stability constant at 1.000 for all recovering events — no variance to test

interpretation.finding: CCS has basin structure without fixed-point convergence dynamics
interpretation.detail: Basin boundary prediction (P2) confirms attractor-like region structure. But P1 failure means the system doesn't converge geometrically to a unique fixed point — it stays in the basin while being continually perturbed by new input.
interpretation.reframe: 2605.12466 fixed-point attractor is wrong model class. CCS is a stochastic attractor — basin stability under continual perturbation, not convergence to a static fixed point. The system orbits within the basin, it doesn't converge.
interpretation.implication: The ecological margin (0.921) measures basin width, not convergence speed. Structural stability is a topological property (staying in the basin), not a dynamical one (rate of return to fixed point).

verdict: CHALLENGED — 1/3 predictions pass. Basin structure real, fixed-point dynamics absent. Fit is partially decorative: the BASIN part of attractor theory maps, the FIXED-POINT part doesn't.
